senses.definition: A fisher, a person engaged in fishing:

subsenses.definition: Any person who attempts to catch fish.

quotes.text: Ivor had acquired more than a mile of fishing rights with the house ; he was not at all a good fisherman, but one must do something ; one generally, however, banged a ball with a squash-racket against a wall.
quotes.reference: 1922, Michael Arlen, “3/19/2”, in “Piracy”: A Romantic Chronicle of These Days:

subsenses.definition: A person whose profession is catching fish.
examples: He is a fisherman, out on a trawler for days at a time.

quotes.text: I knovv God by Miracle can inſtruct Kings, as he rained Mannah, and raiſed the Apoſtles from letterless Fiſher-men, to learned Metropolitans, and profound Doctours.
quotes.reference: 1663, Edward Waterhous[e], chapter I, in Fortescutus Illustratus; or A Commentary on that Nervous Treatise De Laudibus Legum Angliæ, Written by Sir John Fortescue Knight, […], London: […] Tho[mas] Roycroft for Thomas Dicas […], →OCLC, page 38:

quotes.text: Alienated from the clique society, / A lonely boy finds peace in fishing. / His mother says John this is not the way life's supposed to be. / Don't you see the life that you are missing? / And he says / When I grow up I want to be, / One of the harvesters of the sea. / I think before my days are done, / I want to be a fisherman.

senses.definition: A vessel (boat or ship) used for fishing.

quotes.text: They tortured and put to death English factors in the Spice Islands; they descended upon the fisheries of the North Sea in huge fleets escorted by men-of-war that attacked and sank the fishermen of other nations
quotes.reference: 1938, Cecil Ernest Lucas Phillips, Cromwell's Captains, page 196:

quotes.text: Such boats should not have been fast, but the better fishermen — particularly John Alden's designs - […] won a big share of the offshore and coastwise races
